Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Recap of ask:
- Primary goal: run FinLytics inference pipelines (summarization + reranking + embeddings) with predictable latency and cost.
- Estimated active users: 10k weekly active; peak concurrency ~120 concurrent requests.
- Typical prompt length: 1k tokens; responses ~300 tokens.
- Target latency P95: <350ms for short completions, <800ms for longer analytic jobs.

2) Important cost/volume numbers you mentioned on the call:
- Estimated throughput: ~6M tokens/day (burst to 10M/day during reporting windows).
- Baseline monthly volume: ~180M tokens/month; expected growth to ~600M/month in 6–9 months.
- Target unit economics: trying to keep infra + infra margin near $1,000 per 1M tokens (is that right per our brief?).

3) Dedicated capacity specifics we discussed to qualify pricing:
- GPU type: preference for H100 if possible for throughput, fallback A100 80GB.
- Reserved capacity size: initial ask was 2–4 GPUs (pool) to meet sustained throughput; consider burst nodes for spikes.
- Throughput targets: target sustained tokens/sec per GPU ~8–12k (model dependent); peak bursts to 30k+ tokens/sec across pool.

Next steps
- Can you confirm the monthly token target range (low/expected/high) and any blackout windows for reporting spikes?
- I will loop in Marcus (solutions engineering) for a short sizing/pricing calc and Marissa for commercial terms.
- Please attach the workload spreadsheet if you have it (upload works) — that will help with exact GPU sizing.

Attaching a short template for workload metrics — feel free to drop your numbers.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — follow-up & pricing info (GPU type, throughput, tokens)

All — quick sizing + ballpark numbers after reviewing the sheet. Assumptions: Llama-3-70B optimized, mixed request sizes (1k in / 300 out avg), batching & KV cache active. Pricing below is infra-only estimate; ops/support and SLA add-ons on top.

Option A — H100 reserved pool:
- 2x H100: Sustained throughput ~18–24k tokens/sec total; peak bursts to ~60k across pool with burst nodes. Good for 150–300M tokens/month sustained; estimated infra cost ~= $5,000/hr reserved equivalent -> monthly reserved cost ~$360,000. Unit economics ~= $1,200 per 1M tokens at 150M/month, improves to ~$430 per 1M at 750M/month with utilization + caching.
- 4x H100: Sustained throughput ~36–48k tokens/sec; supports 300–600M tokens/month; monthly reserved cost ~$700,000. Unit economics ~= $900 per 1M at 350M/month, ~$500 per 1M at 750M/month.
- 8x H100: for full scale; monthly reserved cost ~$1.3M; unit economics drop below $400 per 1M at 750M/month.

Option B — A100 80GB reserved pool (fallback):
- 2x A100: sustained ~14–18k tokens/sec; monthly reserved cost ~$260,000; unit economics ~ $1,700 per 1M at 150M, ~$600 at 750M.
- 4x A100: monthly ~$500,000; unit economics ~ $1,100 per 1M at 350M.

Notes on assumptions and levers:
- These numbers include expected gains from KV prefix caching and batching; workloads with higher cache hit rates will be materially cheaper.
- We typically include a small burst pool (on-demand) for the 2–6 hour spikes — billed separately on usage.
- We can build a blended committed plan that targets their $700–$1,200/1M range at 350M+/month by committing to 4x H100 + 20% commit on burst usage + a 12-month term.

I'll prepare a short one-pager with a 2/4/8 GPU table and estimated unit economics across low/expected/high bands for procurement.

– Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
